title: Amazon S3 Overview
description: Understand S3 buckets, objects, storage classes, and how they fit ASP.NET Core apps.

data.text: Amazon S3 is an object storage service that stores data as objects in buckets. It is the workhorse of AWS storage and is used for uploads, static assets, backups, and data lakes.

data.title: Core concepts
items: **Bucket** — a top-level container with a globally unique name
**Object** — a file and its metadata stored in a bucket
**Key** — the full path to an object inside a bucket
**Storage class** — the performance and cost tier for an object

data.title: Create an S3 bucket with AWS CLI
data.content:
Use the AWS CLI to create the infrastructure.

data.title: Bucket naming
data.text: S3 bucket names must be globally unique across all AWS accounts. Use a prefix like your project name or initials to avoid collisions.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: S3 stores objects in globally unique buckets
Storage classes balance cost and access speed
S3 is the default choice for files in new ASP.NET Core apps
Use the AWS CLI or C# SDK to manage buckets and objects
data.takeaway: S3 is the foundation of AWS storage. Start with S3 Standard and move objects to cheaper classes as they age.
